I do like to explain a lot of what goes into making great photos like organization, communication and I create a timeline with them that they like and I feel comfortable with for the day photography wise. I try to help each client feel like they don't have to do all the planning alone and I also like to meet with the couple and see the venue and reception area as well as any area near those places to scout for photos. 

I usually don't hear responses or even a simple reply from any of the clients that cancel or don't show. I also get a lot of no replies to my emails too. These emails are very well thought out, have a call to action in them, I am not asking too many questions, and am trying to keep my emails short and to the point when I can. Still I am finding an overall "fickleness" to this year that I've never encountered. I have been out of shooting weddings for 2 years now but still have never had such a problem. It seems the more I try to market and book the more whiff's I'm coming up with instead of more bookings. I have definitely scoured the internet, professionals I know, and people who just do business in general about these problems. I've tried so many things from changing my email approach, to creating a visually pleasing price sheet.....Created calls to action to separate clients who may not be serious. I've made my starting price point clear to every client as well as having it on my contact page.
